1.title: The language, the tools and the first web app
back: This book starts at zero: no programming before, only a computer. Chapter by chapter, you write PHP that runs, and you see what it prints.
Every example in the book is a real file, tested on every change, with the output it really gives. Each chapter adds to one project, Shelf, a small library app, so what you learn is used at once.
points: the language: variables, arrays, functions, types and errors
objects: classes, interfaces, enums and value objects
the tools: Composer, tests, static analysis, Git and Docker
the web: forms, sessions, CSRF and file uploads
databases: SQL, PDO, transactions and migrations
1.next: Volume 2 makes Shelf secure, gives it an API, moves it to Symfony and puts it online.

2.title: Secure web applications, from Symfony to production
back: This book goes on where Volume 1 ends: Shelf is a working web app with a database. Now it gets the things a real application needs.
Every example in the book is a real file, tested on every change, with the output it really gives. At the end, Shelf is finished: a library app that a real library could run.
points: security: passwords, login, roles, and the common attacks
a REST API with tokens, pagination and tests
Symfony: routing, Twig, Doctrine, forms and security
production: configuration, logging, CI and deployment
the finished app: search, accounts, lending, reminders, three languages
2.next: Volume 1 covers the language, the tools and the first web app, from zero.
